text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Thursday that it is recalling 7,274 Toyota Cavalier cars produced by General Motors Corp (GM) to fix an engine control computer system.
The recall affects models imported between October 24, 1995, and June 24, 1996. The cars were made at GM's Rosetown factory in Ohio for sale in Japan.
Repair costs are estimated to total 70 million yen, a Toyota spokeswoman said.
The fault in the computer system could cause stalling or an unstable revolution of the car engine.
Toyota started selling Cavaliers in Japan in January this year with an annual sales target of 20,000 units. Total sales stood at 9,647 Cavaliers as of December 10.
No accidents have been reported as a result of the defect, the spokeswoman said.
